response.sql: SELECT o.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, COUNT(*) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.bandusagepct > 47.6 GROUP BY o.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Moon phase comes from observatories.lunarstage, a station-level attribute, so every telescope at a station takes that station's phase. observationalconditions is not used.
The inner JOIN drops telescopes whose observstation has no match in observatories, as the request specifies.
Telescopes with a NULL lunarstage are kept and form their own NULL moon_phase group. The request does not say to exclude them.
The count is the number of telescopes (telescregistry is the primary key, so COUNT(*) over the joined rows counts each telescope once).

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude telescopes whose observatory has no recorded moon phase (lunarstage IS NULL), so only real phase values are grouped.
alternatives.sql: SELECT o.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, COUNT(*) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.bandusagepct > 47.6 AND o.lunarstage IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC LIMIT 10;
